correctness.rationale: A complete finite and asymptotic argument is present. The known vertex formula yields rank frequencies. Nonnegative coordinates give a diameter equality iff both endpoints have full rank and disjoint support. Uniform permutations give exact first two conditional moments; overlapping-support hypergeometric factorial moments yield the Poisson count, and fixed-size without-replacement label samples yield independent uniform marks. Full-rank probability tends to one; Markov/Chebyshev handle the other regimes. The package verifier re-enumerates all finite pairs in eight small cases and checks each exact formula.

value.rationale: The previously known diameter measures only a worst-case pair. The exact probability that uniform random vertices attain it has a sharp birthday threshold, and the continuously marked compound-Poisson law determines a natural near-diameter metric distribution with nontrivial jump density and moment information. It is a motivated structural two-point geometric law, not a restatement of a facet count or an edge length.
